findings.title: Falsehood as stripped ornament
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus falsehood behaves like a beautified surface whose apparent continuity lasts only until testing strips it and exposes a barren substrate.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how an attractive claim may persist as a surface while the pericope's test exposes what lies underneath.
findings.containment: This is a material analogy for exposure over time, not the ordinary lexical meaning of falsehood and not a claim that every decorated surface is deceptive. The simpler reading that the lie fails a truth test remains intact.

findings.title: The added world-collective contact
findings.claim: The explicitly added 1:2 supplies a distinct same-root overlay: the focus's denied knowledge is heard beside the name for the world and created beings as a whole, without changing the focus word's local knowledge meaning.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier at 18:5:5 contacts the external occurrence at 1:2:4, where the same root appears in the worlds-and-created-beings branch; that external word supplies a concrete creation-order field that the focus claim cannot turn into knowledge by assertion.
findings.reader_payoff: The added overlay makes the contrast between a named created whole and an unsupported claim of knowledge perceptible while leaving the focus ayah recoverable on its own terms.
findings.containment: This is the only retained external delta. It does not make the focus form mean worlds, import the general themes of 1:3-1:7, or treat the added ayat as an implicit whole-surah reading.

epistemic.reason: The external Arabic surface and the accepted focus branch are supplied exactly, but no HFT or connection support is attached; the relation is therefore a bounded contextual resonance only.
